subsystems.name: Microdisplay
subsystems.role: projects digital images onto the retina without blocking the view of the world.

subsystems.name: Power and data link
subsystems.role: receives power and data wirelessly from an external wearable.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: drives the display and processes sensor signals.

subsystems.name: Sensors
subsystems.role: tracks eye movements and head orientation for stable image placement.

subsystems.name: Lens body and encapsulation
subsystems.role: protects the electronics from tears and the eye from the electronics, while letting oxygen through.

buildSteps.title: Design the layout
buildSteps.detail: Engineers map where the micro-LEDs, circuits and coil must sit on a curved, millimetre-thin surface, and simulate how light will reach the retina.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the microdisplay
buildSteps.detail: Micro-LEDs are grown on a semiconductor wafer, etched to micrometre size, then transferred onto a flexible, transparent substrate.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: Driver chips, sensors and a tiny inductive coil are bonded to the substrate and connected with fine conductive traces.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: The assembly is coated with a biocompatible, oxygen-permeable polymer that seals out moisture and ions.

buildSteps.title: Mould the lens
buildSteps.detail: The encapsulated stack is embedded in a silicone hydrogel and cured in a mould that gives it the curvature and optical power of a contact lens.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Bench tests check power, heat and image quality; then animal and human trials assess comfort, safety and visual performance.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Automated pick-and-place, coating and moulding lines would be needed to make lenses consistently at low cost.

prerequisites.why: they can be bright enough to be seen in daylight while using very little power, but making them on a flexible, curved lens is not yet routine.
inductive coupling works in many devices, but shrinking it to fit on a lens without overheating the eye is a challenge.
the eye is sensitive to foreign materials, so the electronics must be perfectly sealed for years.
they keep the image stable and the power draw low enough to avoid uncomfortable heating.

pathway.milestone: laboratory prototypes with simple displays or sensors, tested in animals
pathway.unlocks: proof that electronics can survive on a lens and be powered wirelessly.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials for medical uses such as vision correction or continuous monitoring
pathway.unlocks: safety data and a regulatory route for active contact lenses.

pathway.milestone: consumer AR lenses with basic text and icon overlays
pathway.unlocks: hands-free navigation and notifications for everyday wear.

pathway.milestone: full-field, all-day AR contact lenses with rich imagery
pathway.unlocks: seamless augmented reality without glasses or headsets.
